assessment:
Four wishes, and three of them put the card on top rather than in hand: Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn and Enlightened Tutor book your next draw. All three are instants, so cast them at an opponent's end step and the appointment costs no tempo. Huatli, Poet of Unity is the fourth: her front face hands you a basic, and her saga's third chapter puts a Dinosaur in hand three upkeeps after you pay to flip her.

The arithmetic that decides most wishes. Gishath, Sun's Avatar casts at a mean of turn 7.362 and is on the battlefield by turn six in 25.5% of goldfish games. Three cards make a command-zone cast cheaper — Otepec Huntmaster {1}, Urza's Incubator {2}, Knight of the Stampede {2} — and together they leave {R}{G}{W}. Worldly Tutor and Congregation reach the two creatures, Enlightened Tutor reaches the artifact, and each is 7.1% of an opening seven on its own. When turn four arrives with no reducer drawn, that is the wish.

The second use is the reveal itself. Congregation at Dawn puts three creature cards on top in your order; Gishath reveals as many cards as he dealt, and every Dinosaur creature card among them enters. No stack has resolved a stacked reveal, so the sequence rests on the trigger's text, not on a checked board. The third use is the one-sided sweep: Blasphemous Act plus Temple Altisaur is drawn together in 8.1% of games and tutor-assisted in 29.9% (goldfish targets), which is the largest lift a wish buys in this deck.

What no wish reaches: an instant or a sorcery. Hold the Act and fetch the Altisaur, never the reverse.

targets.scenario: End of the turn before your third, one green source untapped. Your hand is lands and Dinosaurs at four and five mana; nothing in it or on your board makes a command-zone cast cheaper.
targets.why: Buy the largest discount a creature tutor can reach. Knight takes {2} off every Dinosaur spell you cast, your commander included; with Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator beside it he costs {R}{G}{W}. The goldfish reads him cast by turn six in 25.5% of games and never by turn ten in 2,299 of 10,000; a reducer on turn four is how you land on the right side of that. Knight is a Human Knight, so the reveal bottoms it — a wish or a draw are the only ways it arrives. Cast the tutor at their end step, draw the Knight, play it on four.

citations.quote: a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven
Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists

targets.scenario: Blasphemous Act is in your hand. Two opponents have gone wide — a dozen creatures across the table — and your board is three Dinosaurs and six lands.
targets.why: This is the wish that moves a figure. The Act plus the Altisaur is drawn together in 8.1% of games and tutor-assisted in 29.9%; you hold one half, so the other half is one wish away. Stack 004 is the record: the Act costs {R} off nine creatures, every other Dinosaur you control is dealt 1 and survives, the Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself and takes 13, and with Wrathful Raptors out the wreckage is 16 at a player. Fetch, draw, cast the Altisaur on five, sweep the turn after. Two turns, and the table has to see the 3/4 as a threat to stop it.

citations.quote: commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further

targets.scenario: You are ahead. Five bodies on the battlefield under Garruk's Uprising, the seat to your left at 14 with two 2/2s and no untapped mana.
targets.why: Take the cheapest twelve power in the deck and close. Ghalta costs {X} less where X is your creatures' total power, and the goldfish reads mean board power 31.555 on turn 8 — she is {G}{G}. Uprising already gives her trample. Wish at their end step, draw her, cast her precombat, swing. No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing in this deck, so the kill is arithmetic against their blockers, not a verified line; count them before you commit.

citations.quote: count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Gishath is castable next turn. The seat you will attack holds up mana every turn and has flashed in a blocker twice this game.
targets.why: The wish nobody reads. Sunwing says creatures your opponents control enter tapped, and a blocker has to be untapped when blockers are declared — so whatever they flash in at your declare-attackers step arrives tapped and stands there. Three mana, a 2/3 flyer, and the lane is open the turn he swings. Forge's connect rate was 0.70 per attack; Sunwing is for the seat that made the other 0.30. Draw it, play it a turn before him, say nothing.

tutors.notes: The card goes on top, so a wish cast in your main phase is a turn of warning. Cast it at their end step. When mana rather than ignition is the problem, Selvala, Heart of the Wilds is the fetch: {G} and a tap for mana equal to your greatest power, which Gishath makes seven.

targets.scenario: Gishath is on the battlefield with Pantlaza, Sun-Favored beside him. The seat to your left is tapped low with one blocker he tramples over. It is their end step and you hold {G}{G}{W}.
targets.why: Load the reveal. Three creature cards on top in your order; when he connects for 7, every Dinosaur creature card among the seven enters. Put Dreadmaw first, Vaultborn Tyrant second, Regisaur Alpha third. All three enter as one event, so each sees the others: Dreadmaw draws a card per other Dinosaur you control, Vaultborn draws and gains 3 for itself and for each entering creature with power 4 or more, Alpha hands the new board haste and a 3/3. Pantlaza discovers once — stack it to resolve on Dreadmaw or Vaultborn, both 6/6, for X=6. No stack has resolved this exact board; the counts rest on the cards' text and the rule that checks every newcomer for its triggers.

citations.quote: Each time an event puts one or more permanents onto the battlefield, all permanents on the battlefield (including the newcomers) are checked for any enters-the-battlefield triggers that match the event.
count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: A wrath has just resolved. You untap into six lands and an empty board, Gishath is in the command zone with one recast tax on him, and the table has moved on to the seat that still has creatures.
targets.why: Rebuild through the payoff that needs no combat and no eight mana. Pantlaza discovers X equal to the toughness of each Dinosaur that enters, once a turn, so every body you cast from here is a body and a card. Take two cards here, not three — Pantlaza first, a five-toughness Dinosaur second — and leave your third draw live. Recasting Gishath is eight plus {2}; this is five. From stack 001: when a Dinosaur enters beside a token maker, let the discover resolve before the token enters or you take the small X.

targets.scenario: Two opponents have gone wide with tokens and utility creatures. You control three Dinosaurs, three white sources, and more mana than plays.
targets.why: Take the answer nobody expects from the beatdown seat. Wakening destroys all non-Dinosaur creatures only if you cast it from your hand — off the reveal or a Portal it is a 7/7 and nothing more — so top it, draw it, cast it. Count white first: {5}{W}{W}{W} off 17 white land sources, 21 with rocks, is the steepest colour ask in the deck, and white comes on curve 61.0% of the time with rocks and dorks. Make this wish only when three white sources are already on the table.

citations.quote: killing the scariest creature instead of the one that beats you

targets.scenario: The seat across from you is an equipment deck: three activations a turn, a fetchland every other turn, and nobody at the table is drawing extra cards.
targets.why: The wish nobody sees. Armasaur draws you a card whenever an opponent activates an ability of a creature or land that is not a mana ability — equip, a fetch, a crew, a Rogue's Passage of their own. Against that seat it is a 2/5 that draws two or three a turn for {1}{G}{G}. The goldfish cannot see it: Armasaur is named in draw_not_modelled, and its 1.353 extra cards by turn 8 is a floor that excludes this card entirely. Put it on top behind whatever you need this turn and let it work for the rest of the game.

tutors.notes: You choose the order, so choose it as a schedule: card one is this turn's promise, cards two and three are your next two draws. It says up to three; take two whenever a live draw is worth more than a known one. Three Dinosaurs on top the turn before he connects is the reveal pre-loaded, and it is a reading of the trigger's text, not a verified line.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three with one white source untapped. Your hand is Dinosaurs at four and five mana and no cost reducer has shown.
targets.why: Fix the whole hand rather than the next card. Name Dinosaur: every Dinosaur creature spell costs {2} less across 30 of your 34 creature entries, and your commander drops to six. This is the one reducer of the three that a creature tutor cannot reach, and the artifact wish is the only one that finds it. Against a mean cast turn of 7.362, two mana off every Dinosaur for the rest of the game outweighs any single body.

citations.quote: k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of *every* card

targets.scenario: Turn one on the play, a white source in hand and this beside it.
targets.why: Buy the earliest mana you will ever buy. The goldfish reads mean available mana 2.143 on turn 2; Sol Ring makes that four, and every turn after compounds. Forge cast it 10 times in 40 games — the most of any rock. Cast the tutor at the end of turn one, draw the Ring on two, and the whole curve moves a turn.

targets.scenario: Mid-game. Your hand is nearly empty after trading in an early skirmish, one four-power Dinosaur is still on the battlefield, and Gishath is two turns away.
targets.why: Buy the grind. Uprising replaces itself on entry with a four-power creature out, draws on every four-power creature that enters afterwards — stack 001 counted three draws off one reveal — and gives the whole board trample, which is what turns their chump blocks into damage when he swings. Extra cards drawn by turn 8 reads 1.353 in the goldfish; this is the card that moves it.

targets.scenario: The blue seat has held counter mana for three turns and two of your threats have died on the stack. Your hand is Dinosaurs you cannot resolve.
targets.why: Stop casting spells at them. Resolve the Portal naming Dinosaur, and {3} plus a tap puts a Dinosaur from your hand onto the battlefield — no cast, nothing to counter, at instant speed on their end step. Mind the mana: Secluded Courtyard's clause says 'or activate an ability' and pays the {3}; Unclaimed Territory pays creature spells only and does not. It does nothing for the commander in the zone.

citations.quote: hold single-target removal until the threat is pointed at you

tutors.notes: Your only wish that reaches a noncreature permanent, so do not spend it on a body. Two more calls when the board asks: Descendants' Path when your hand is empty and your board is Dinosaurs, and Mirari's Wake when the plan is one enormous turn.

tutors.card: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

targets.scenario: Huatli enters on turn three off green mana. You hold Trapjaw Tyrant and Wakening Sun's Avatar with one white source on the battlefield.
targets.why: Take the colour you are short. White has 17 land sources against green's 22, and lands alone put white on curve 48.1% of the time, the lowest of your three colours. Trapjaw wants {W}{W}, Wakening {W}{W}{W}. Her search puts the basic in hand, a guaranteed land drop rather than a draw you might miss. Default here and deviate only when the hand argues.

citations.quote: Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists

targets.scenario: You are two turns from casting Gishath. Your lands make green and white and you control exactly one red source.
targets.why: Fetch the pip the plan is missing. He wants {R}{G}{W} together and red has 18 land sources, on curve 51.5% of the time from lands alone. Take the Mountain and cast him on schedule; a turn-eight cast with the colours beats a turn-seven hand that cannot pay.

targets.scenario: Roar of the Fifth People reaches chapter three at your upkeep. The blue seat has held counter mana every turn and your last two threats died on the stack.
targets.why: Take the one they cannot touch. Chapter three puts any Dinosaur card in your hand; Carnage Tyrant cannot be countered and has hexproof, so cast it into their open mana. One upkeep later chapter four gives your Dinosaurs double strike and trample, and a 7/6 with double strike is fourteen.

citations.quote: hold single-target removal until the threat is pointed at you

targets.scenario: Chapter three triggers with three Dinosaurs on the battlefield and chapter two turning your creatures into mana. One opponent is at 20 with two blockers.
targets.why: Close on the schedule you set three upkeeps ago. Ghalta costs {X} less where X is your creatures' total power, and chapter two's creature mana pays what is left, so she lands the turn you wish for her. Chapter four then gives everything double strike and trample: a 12/12 with double strike is twenty-four through two blockers. Plan the flip so chapter four lands on the turn you swing.

tutors.notes: The real quest is the transformation: pay {3} and two hybrid at sorcery speed and start the countdown — two 3/3s, then creature mana, then the Dinosaur wish, then double strike and trample. On the land side, if Wayward Swordtooth is out the basic she hands you is played the same turn as your normal drop; take a Forest there, since 39 of your cards carry a green pip.

gaps: No wish finds an instant or a sorcery. Blasphemous Act is unreachable, so the one-sided sweep is only ever half-tutored: hold the Act and fetch Temple Altisaur, never the reverse. The same hole covers protection — Flawless Maneuver, Akroma's Will, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm and Eerie Interlude are held by turn six in 51.1% of games and no wish moves that number.

Ignition has three cards and two routes. Worldly Tutor and Congregation reach Otepec Huntmaster and Knight of the Stampede; Enlightened Tutor reaches Urza's Incubator; Huatli's chapter three reaches none of them, since none is a Dinosaur. Spend both routes elsewhere and the commander arrives when he arrives: mean turn 7.362.

Every wish here is a delivery, not an arrival. Three tutors put the card on top, one draw away, so against a seat holding sweeper mana the wish can die in transit. Cast the instants at an end step to cut the exposure to zero turns.
Huatli's entry search finds basic lands only. Treat her front face as fixing and expect no Dinosaur from her until chapter three, three upkeeps after you pay to flip her.

Stack 001's stipulated reveal and stack 004's board each carry a card that has left the 99 (Ripjaw Raptor, Cultivate). The rules in both hold for any Dinosaurs of the same power and toughness; the Congregation line above that stacks Dreadmaw, Vaultborn and Alpha is unresolved and is queued as a stack scenario.
